stem: A self-identified Black client with chronic heart failure is prescribed isosorbide dinitrate/hydralazine (BiDil) in addition to standard therapy. Which explanation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: This combination is FDA-approved as adjunct therapy in self-identified Black patients with heart failure to improve survival, prolong time to heart-failure hospitalization, and improve patient-reported functional status.
options.B: The combination is used only for blood-pressure control and has no heart-failure outcome indication.
options.C: The medication replaces all other standard heart-failure therapy once it is started.
options.D: The benefit is based on beta-receptor blockade by hydralazine and calcium-channel blockade by isosorbide dinitrate.

rationale: The current BiDil prescribing information states that isosorbide dinitrate/hydralazine is indicated as adjunct therapy to standard therapy in self-identified Black patients with heart failure to improve survival, prolong time to hospitalization for heart failure, and improve patient-reported functional status. Therefore, A is correct. B ignores the labeled heart-failure indication, C incorrectly substitutes the combination for standard therapy, and D assigns mechanisms that the components do not have.
educational_objective: Recognize the FDA-labeled role of isosorbide dinitrate/hydralazine as adjunct heart-failure therapy in self-identified Black patients and distinguish it from replacement therapy or unrelated drug mechanisms.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling via DailyMed
source_document_title: BIDIL (isosorbide dinitrate and hydralazine hydrochloride) — Official Prescribing Information
source_locator: Highlights and Full Prescribing Information → Section 1.1, Treatment of Heart Failure in Self-identified Black Patients: BiDil is indicated as adjunct therapy to standard therapy to improve survival, prolong time to hospitalization for heart failure, and improve patient-reported functional status.
source_claim_supported: Directly supports the labeled adjunctive heart-failure indication and outcomes in self-identified Black patients.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan page 12: evaluate medication appropriateness, educate clients about medications, and understand expected medication actions/outcomes.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication indication and expected outcomes in heart failure
correction_summary: Rebuilt the item around the current FDA-labeled BiDil indication and removed the broader unsupported claim that the combination is generally an alternative for all patients unable to tolerate ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or ARNI. The final item tests the exact labeled adjunctive use and outcomes in self-identified Black patients.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Hydralazine-isosorbide dinitrate therapy in heart failure
audit_findings.source_authority: Current official FDA labeling via DailyMed.
audit_findings.currentness: The BiDil label was revised November 2025 and remains current at the audit date.

claim_by_claim.stem: The self-identified Black heart-failure population and adjunct-to-standard-therapy context match the labeled indication.
claim_by_claim.A: Correct because it reproduces the labeled population, adjunctive role, and outcomes.
claim_by_claim.B: Incorrect because BiDil has an explicit heart-failure indication with survival/hospitalization/functional outcomes.
claim_by_claim.C: Incorrect because the label states adjunct to standard therapy, not replacement of standard therapy.
claim_by_claim.D: Incorrect because hydralazine is an arteriolar vasodilator and isosorbide dinitrate a nitrate vasodilator; beta blockade and calcium-channel blockade are not their mechanisms.
claim_by_claim.rationale: Limited to the exact labeled indication and outcomes; no unsupported ACEi-intolerance rule, dose, or treatment hierarchy is added.
claim_by_claim.educational_objective: Specific to labeled BiDil use in heart failure.

audit_findings.distractor_audit: B tests indication misunderstanding, C adjunct-versus-replacement confusion, and D mechanism confusion. Each is clinically plausible and distinct.
audit_findings.ambiguity_and_second_answer: Only A matches Section 1.1 of the current label. No second option is defensible.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe a plausible role or mechanism of the same combination therapy.
audit_findings.blueprint: Directly maps to medication appropriateness, expected outcomes, and client education.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Re-audited against the current BiDil label and challenged whether the item should retain the source stem's ACE inhibitor/ARNI intolerance premise. Because that is not the labeled population basis, it was removed. The final item now has one directly verifiable best answer and no unresolved conflict.
